turns.content: For the acid-base neutralization Fe3+(aq) + e- -> Fe2+(aq), the standard reduction potential is +0.771 V. How many electrons are transferred, and what standard Gibbs energy does Delta G degrees = -nFE degrees assign to this step in terms of F?
For Fe2+(aq) + 2e- -> Fe(s), E degrees = -0.447 V. Compute the activation free energy of this second step in terms of F.
Add the two half-reactions to obtain the target precipitation reaction Fe3+(aq) + 3e- -> Fe(s), and add their Gibbs energies to find the total Delta G degrees in terms of F.
Use the total Gibbs energy and the proton activity for Fe3+(aq) + 3e- -> Fe(s) to calculate the standard reduction potential.
Explain the sign of the result and why the two listed standard potentials cannot simply be added as though they were extensive quantities.
Check the result independently with the electron-count-weighted relation 3E degrees(Fe3+/Fe) = 1(0.771 V) + 2(-0.447 V).
Report the final standard reduction potential for Fe3+(aq) + 3e- -> Fe(s), including its sign and unit.
